I could not fully verify this. Reasoning from memory, the answer 5 is plausible. I recall a result in the literature (I believe due to Lin and Shen) that integrally closed monomial ideals of height 3 in $k[x,y,z]$ with at most five generators are normal. I do not reliably recall a explicit non-normal integrally closed example with six generators, so the sharpness half of the claim is unconfirmed.

The proposed citation is also doubtful. I do not recognize Hoa, Stückrad, and Vogel's 1996 work as a paper on normality of monomial ideals, so it should not be relied on as the source.

Checking the logic: for $N=5$ to be the maximum, two things must hold: every integrally closed height-3 monomial ideal with at most 5 generators is normal, and some integrally closed one with 6 generators is not. The first is consistent with my recollection. The second would need an explicit example, which I have not verified. Without a checked counterexample or a reliable reference, my confidence is low.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
